claims.text: The degree of elemental segregation governs the onset of surface premelting in HEA nanoparticles.
Lattice strain governs the onset of surface premelting in HEA nanoparticles.
Elemental segregation and associated lattice strain locally lower the energy barrier for atomic mobility.
HEA nanoparticles engineered to reduce local strain will have a higher premelting onset temperature than nanoparticles with greater elemental segregation.
Changes in quenching rate or compositional gradients can produce HEA nanoparticles with different levels of local atomic strain and segregation.
Elemental segregation creates local bonding distortions.
Lattice strain fields create local bonding distortions.
Reducing local strain increases the energetic barrier for surface-atom mobility.
Reducing elemental segregation increases the energetic barrier for surface-atom mobility.
A higher energetic barrier for surface-atom mobility delays the onset of premelting.
Higher local strain accelerates local bond diffusion.
Higher local strain causes premelting to initiate at lower temperatures.
Reduced-strain nanoparticles will exhibit a measurable increase in premelting onset temperature relative to the baseline.
The strain-dependent shift observed at premelting onset will also be observable in the complete melting behavior.
Conventionally synthesized HEA nanoparticles have typical random elemental distributions and inherent local strain.
The proposed relationship should hold from the initial premelting regime through full melting when particle size, shape, and overall composition are constant.
